final_report.summary: Cycle 1 established the hybrid production architecture end-to-end: RESEARCH genre calls were parallelized with asyncio.gather and routed to Claude Haiku, psychology research remained on Claude Sonnet, downstream ROLES/OUTLINE/MATRIX/PROFILES were pinned to Sonnet, and project creation was locked to claude/sonnet with provider/model controls removed from UI. Cycle 2 then hardened and validated that baseline for production readiness: deterministic input sanitization and bounds were added for story title/genres/concept lines before prompt/file use, RESEARCH gained explicit per-genre attempt diagnostics and isolated retry observability, adversarial expectations were aligned to lock-and-ignore semantics, and functional/spec/adversarial/mutation validation artifacts were regenerated. Final evidence includes real 4-genre run telemetry showing concurrent behavior (wall-clock materially below summed attempt durations) and fresh Firefox :99 screenshots confirming provider/model controls remain absent and create flow still works.
key_achievements: Parallel genre research implemented and operationalized with Haiku subagents plus Sonnet psychology sequencing.
Production model policy enforced: project creation locked to provider=claude and model=sonnet while inbound overrides are ignored.
Core generation stages (ROLES, OUTLINE, MATRIX, PROFILES) pinned internally to Sonnet for quality consistency.
Security hardening added for user-controlled research inputs with deterministic normalization and bounded sanitization.
RESEARCH observability upgraded with per-genre attempt timelines/error context and isolated retry semantics.
Validation suite completed with passing functional/spec alignment/adversarial checks and 100% mutation score on target tests.
Firefox :99 UI regression evidence captured showing provider/model controls remain removed and create flow remains functional.
Parallelism evidence documented from real workflow telemetry (concurrency factor consistent with concurrent execution).
challenges_overcome: Resolved policy mismatch in adversarial expectations by shifting from reject-on-override to ignore-and-lock semantics.
Handled transient external Claude CLI failures during real run while still extracting reliable concurrency/attempt telemetry evidence.
Improved diagnosability of RESEARCH failures by replacing ambiguous stage-level failure reporting with explicit per-genre attempt traces.
Added hardening without regressing stage transitions, token accounting, or hybrid routing behavior.
lessons_learned: Locking model policy is strongest when enforced at API persistence boundaries and mirrored by UI removal of mutable controls.
Parallel pipelines need per-task retry isolation and per-task diagnostics; global retries obscure root cause and inflate latency.
Input sanitization for LLM workflows should be deterministic and bounded, but preserve semantic payload to avoid output-quality regressions.
End-to-end timing and log artifacts are essential to prove real concurrency when external dependencies are noisy.
Combining functional/spec/adversarial/mutation checks provides better production confidence than any single test modality.
